props.name: Claim: activity
props.statement: ZnO and Al2O3 addition increases the catalytic activity and the stability, and the CuZnAl oxide catalysts reach industrially relevant current densities (up to 90 mA/cm2).

props.name: Claim: diffusion
props.scope: over the potential range of the Rdiff chart, p. 5
props.statement: Diffusion is less hindered on CuZA-06-03-01 than on CuZ-06-03 and Cu-06: its diffusional resistance (Rdiff) is the lowest of the three catalysts over the measured potential range (about -1.35 to -0.40 V vs RHE).

props.name: Claim: oxygenates
props.scope: at -1.39, -1.14 and -0.89 V vs RHE, as read from the p. 5 faradaic-efficiency charts
props.statement: During CO2 electroreduction in CO2-saturated KHCO3 (25 °C, 1 bar), all three Cu-Zn-Al-based oxide catalysts produce C1 to C3 oxygenated products and syngas (H2 and CO); the faradaic-efficiency charts also show methane and, on Cu-06, methanol and 2-propanol among the products.

props.name: Claim: role
props.scope: as tabulated for the as-prepared powders, p. 4
props.statement: Adding ZnO and then Al2O3 raises the BET surface area (18.4 -> 55.16 -> 101.65 m2 g-1), disperses the Cu active phase and cuts the CuO crystallite size below 10 nm (17 -> 7 -> 9 nm), while the superficial Cu0+Cu1+ share falls from 22 % to 8 % and 5 %.

props.name: Claim: standardized
props.note: asserted on the methods slide without supporting data in the deck
props.statement: The co-precipitation synthesis method has been fully standardized.

props.name: Claim: syngas
props.scope: p. 8 (H2/CO and JCO charts at -1.39, -1.14, -0.89 V vs RHE)
props.statement: The Cu-Zn-Al oxide catalysts are more selective towards syngas (H2 and CO) formation than bare Cu, and with CuZA-06-03-01 the H2/CO ratio is tuneable by changing the applied potential.
